title: Add Business Days to Date: how it works, formula and examples

content:
The [Add Business Days to Date](/add-business-days-to-date) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Add business days to a date, skipping weekends and holidays. Enter your start date, business days to add and holidays to skip (one date per line, YYYY-MM-DD) and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Add business days to a date, skipping Saturdays and Sundays — and any holidays you list. Delivery estimates, contract deadlines, invoice terms and project plans are usually counted in business days, not calendar days: “5 business days from Friday” lands the following Friday, not Wednesday. Enter the start date and how many business days to add; holidays go in one per line as YYYY-MM-DD dates. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers.

## How to use the Add Business Days to Date

Start by picking your start date, then entering your business days to add and finally typing or pasting your holidays to skip (one date per line, YYYY-MM-DD). The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause.

1. Enter the start date and how many business days to add.
2. Optionally list holidays to skip, one date per line (YYYY-MM-DD).
3. Read the result date — and how many calendar and weekend days it spans.

## Formula

Step forward one calendar day at a time, counting only Monday–Friday days that are not listed as holidays. For example, 5 business days from Friday 20 November 2026 is Friday 27 November 2026 — 7 calendar days, with 2 weekend days skipped.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Add Business Days to Date](/add-business-days-to-date) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. Adding 5 business days to Friday 20 November 2026 gives Friday 27 November 2026: the 21st and 22nd are the weekend, so the counted days are the 23rd, 24th, 25th, 26th and 27th. Try the same figures in the [Add Business Days to Date](/add-business-days-to-date) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Start date: 2026-11-20, Business days to add: 5, Holidays to skip (one date per line, YYYY-MM-DD):), the [Add Business Days to Date](/add-business-days-to-date) returns Result date: Friday, November 27, 2026, Business days added: 5, Calendar days: 7, Weekend days skipped: 2. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Age Calculator](/age-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## What counts as a business day

Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays. The start date itself is not counted — “1 business day from Friday” is Monday, not Friday. Different countries and industries have different weekends and holidays (some places work Sundays, some observe Friday as the weekend), so list any extra non-working days in the holidays box to match your own calendar.

## Deadlines and delivery estimates

“Allow 5 business days” is the standard language for deliveries, refunds and contract deadlines precisely because weekends do not count. Count carefully around long weekends: 5 business days before a bank holiday Monday is very different from 5 business days after one. When a deadline matters, add the holidays explicitly rather than assuming them.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- The start date is not counted — day 1 is the next business day.
- List public holidays one per line, as YYYY-MM-DD.
- Check the calendar days too, for planning around weekends.

## Frequently asked questions

### How do I add 5 business days to a date?

Count forward 5 Monday–Friday days, skipping weekends and holidays. 5 business days from Friday 20 November 2026 is Friday 27 November 2026. Try it with your own numbers in the [Add Business Days to Date](/add-business-days-to-date) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Does the start date count?

No. The start date is day zero — the first business day counted is the next working day after it. Try it with your own numbers in the [Add Business Days to Date](/add-business-days-to-date) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Can I skip public holidays too?

Yes — list them in the holidays box, one date per line in YYYY-MM-DD format, and they are skipped like weekends. Try it with your own numbers in the [Add Business Days to Date](/add-business-days-to-date) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What is the difference between business days and calendar days?

Calendar days include weekends; business days are Monday–Friday only. 5 business days usually spans 7 calendar days. Try it with your own numbers in the [Add Business Days to Date](/add-business-days-to-date) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.
